newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Munis marked up 1/2 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Munis marked up 1/2 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were quoted 1/2 point higher in early trade, as June jobs data swept U.S. Treasuries more than a point higher.
"We're marking (bonds) up 1/2," a muni trader said, adding however that activity was "dead" ahead of the July 4th holiday.
A second trader said while his firm was also marking up bonds, activity was starting to improve.
"We just bumped some issues up 1/2 a point," the trader said. "We're marking stuff right now, but we're getting a lot of calls."
The U.S. Labor Department reported that non-farm payrolls grew by 217,000 in June after expanding by a revised 166,000 jobs in May. Economists polled by Reuters had expected a 222,000 rise for June.
"This was right in line," one trader said. "It was exactly what we were looking for."
The benchmark 30-year bond, which had been up about 1/4 point before the report, rose 1-4/32 to 100-1/32 for a 6.62 percent yield.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 31/32 at 118-22/32. The September T-bond contract was up 1-2/32 at 113-4/32. The MOB spread was 178 ticks.

Thursday's actively quoted muni cash issues included Allegheny County, Pa., Sanitary Authority 5-3/8 percent sewer revenue bonds of December 2024. The bonds had a 5.55 percent net bid, versus Wednesday's closing net bid of 5.60 percent.
